provenance: patch 0: toolchain-diff — CL 4.2 evaluates winsock_process_error(wsf(a1,a2,a3,a4), a1,a2,a3,a4) by pushing the outer's four simple args (a4,a3,a2,a1) into callee-saved ebx/esi/edx/eax copies and then RE-PUSHING all four for the inner wsf call (8 pushes + add esp,0x10 + add esp,0x14, 45-47 B). FA instead shares the inner call's 4 push slots with the outer call's args 2..5: after the wsf call the pushed dwords still spell (a1,a2,a3,a4) bottom-up, so only the result is pushed and one add esp,0x14 covers all — 36 B, no callee-saved regs, and a1 is reload-read from its arg slot (mov eax,[esp+8]) between pushes. Tried 6 spellings/flags (nested /O2 /Gy /G5, no /G5, /Ob0, /O2 /Os, /O1, explicit tmp local) — all re-push, no C spelling reproduces the slot sharing, so the body is the FA bytes verbatim (patch replaces all 47 /G5-built CL code bytes; a no-/G5 base is 45 B and leaves 2 stray bytes) with newsites 0x16:6:_w31g_wsf (call ds:[ws+0xe], cdecl fn-ptr slot) and 0x1b:20:_w31g_wproc (rel32, target = next-chunk VA 0x4a2bb0). The wsf call takes (a1,a2,a3,a4); winsock_process_error takes (int result, char*, char*, char*, int).

patch 0 payload imm note: DIR32 newsite site 0x16 supplies symVA (?ws@@3U_winsock_funcs@@A+0xe); the payload's imm dword must carry zeros (payload-zero idiom) or the linker adds the symbol VA on top of the FA literal (0x00577de6 + 0x00577de6 = 0x00aefbcc seen at gate).

patch 0 rel32 note: REL32 newsite site must be the DISP byte (0x1c) and the payload disp carries zeros — linker formula symVA + existing - (site+4); site 0x1b folded the payload's e8 opcode byte into the disp (e8+0x11=0xf9 seen at gate).

Semantics correct in the C even though CL re-pushes; ws_fn = the cdecl fn-ptr slot at ?ws@@3U_winsock_funcs@@A+0xe (0x577de6), winsock_process_error = rel32 next-chunk call. void __cdecl convert_addr_usnf2tcp(sockaddr_in *dst, NET_ADDRESS *src) — writes dst (arg1), reads src (arg2); both structs need only fam@0(word)/port@2(word)/addr@4(dword). Recipe: (1) dword byteswap spelled exactly ((a&0xff00)|(a<<16))<<8 | (((a&0xff0000)|(a>>16))>>8) with a in an unsigned long — CL keeps a in ecx, copies esi/eax, computes (a>>16) by shifting ecx in place (last use), matches and/shl/or schedule verbatim; (2) word byteswap dst->port = ((p&0xff)<<8)|(p>>8) on an unsigned short p stays 16-bit (mov dx,cx / mov dh,dl / mov dl,ch) — the byte-move shuffle, not 32-bit movzx forms; (3) statement order: read p = src->port BEFORE dst->fam = 2 so the fam store (66 c7 word-imm) lands between the port copy and shuffle; (4) no sites/chunk-internal only — no maps beyond the def rename. Sibling twin with w31G_tcp2usnf (same recipe, fam=1 + order fam-first). EXACT first try.

Sibling twin of usnf2tcp (same batch, shared recipe): void __cdecl convert_addr_tcp2usnf(NET_ADDRESS *dst, sockaddr_in *src); differences: dst->fam = 1 FIRST (before the addr read/swap), then addr swap+store, then port read+swap+store; fam value 1 vs 2 and the swap's register cast (ax/cx with mov ch,cl / mov cl,ah in place of dx/cx dh/dl) falls out of the surrounding pressure from the same C text.
